title: HistData timestamps are one hour late in summer: "EST" is not a fixed UTC-5
body:
## Defect

`histdata.py` converts HistData timestamps with a fixed `EST_OFFSET = 5h` (`histdata.py:65`, per HistData's own description "EST without daylight saving"). Measured against a Dukascopy cache of the same instruments, that is wrong for about seven months of every year, in both of HistData's provider eras, and the error is exactly one hour.

## Evidence (2026-10-09, 25 instruments, 2020-01 → 2026-02 against Dukascopy)

- Winter days are **byte-identical** to Dukascopy apart from `volume` (HistData 0.0). E.g. EURUSD 2024-01-10, 2025-03-06, 2025-03-11, 2025-03-27, 2025-10-29, 2025-11-05, 2026-01-14: every minute matches at shift 0.
- Summer days match **only when shifted by −60 min**: EURUSD 2024-06-12 1374/1374 minutes identical at −60 (13 at 0); 2025-04-02 and 2025-10-23 likewise; USA500IDXUSD, XAUUSD, DEUIDXEUR the same.
- The switch dates are the **European** DST dates, not the US ones: 2025-03-11 and 2025-03-27 (US DST on, EU off) match at 0; 2025-04-02 (EU on) is shifted; 2025-10-29 (EU off, US still on until 11-02) matches at 0 again.
- Before 2020 there is no Dukascopy reference, so the check is the FX weekly open, which Dukascopy shows at Sunday 22:00 UTC in winter and 21:00 UTC in summer (17:00 New York). The HistData-derived cache opens at 22:00 UTC in **July** of 2012, 2015, 2018, 2019, 2021 and 2025 (one hour late), and in the US-only DST weeks of March it opens at 22:00 in 2012–2018 (late) but 21:00 in 2019–2025 (correct).

Together: HistData's "EST" is not a fixed UTC−5. For the provider it used until 2018-12-16 the stamps behave as **America/New_York local time including DST**; for the provider since then they behave as **Europe/Zurich local time minus a fixed 6 h** (so they drift with EU DST). Both reduce to "UTC−5 in winter, UTC−4 in summer", with the summer defined by a different calendar in each era.

## Consequences

Every HistData day in the summer months has its minute bars stamped one hour late; daily bars cut on UTC midnight contain the wrong hour at each end; the weekend boundary is off by an hour; and at each DST transition one day in the series has a one-hour gap or overlap. The scale sentry cannot see any of this.

## Fix

In the HistData provider module only (after #81 R1):

- Decode timestamps per era: before the provider switch (2018-12-16; determine the exact boundary from the data, the 0.25-point index grid changes that day) interpret as `America/New_York`; from then on interpret as `Europe/Zurich` after adding 6 h. Implement with `zoneinfo`, not offsets, so the DST rules are the system's. Document the rule and the evidence in the module and README; HistData's own description is wrong and the README should say so.
- Test with synthetic ticks at both DST transitions in both eras, asserting the UTC output, plus a weekly-open test (first tick of a synthetic summer week lands at 21:00 UTC).
- Prove on a real cache with #85: after re-decode, summer days of 2020–2026 must match Dukascopy at shift 0 like the winter ones.
- The existing cache can only be repaired by re-decoding. With #81 R6 (`--keep-raw`) that is local; without it, it is a full re-download. Either way, the fix should ship with a note in the README that HistData caches written before it carry the shift.
